title: A Quiet Room and a Different Question
title_ja: 静かな部屋と別の問い
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の政策、医療指針、教育効果、調査結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: People who describe the quality of a public environment may focus on features that can be measured or observed without asking visitors about their experiences.
sentences.ja: 公共環境の質を述べる人は来訪者に体験を聞かず測定・観察できる特徴に集中することがある。

sentences.en: Such information can be useful, but it may not reveal how people with different needs experience the same place.
sentences.ja: その情報は有用でも、異なる必要を持つ人々が同じ場所をどう経験するか明らかにしないかもしれない。

sentences.en: The distinction is relevant to the design of spaces intended for people who are waiting to receive information or assistance.
sentences.ja: この区別は情報や援助を受けるため待つ人々向けの空間設計に関連する。

sentences.en: A fictional example involving a waiting area illustrates why the apparent comfort of a room may depend partly on the circumstances of its users.
sentences.ja: 待合区域に関する架空例は部屋の見かけの快適さが利用者の事情にも依存し得る理由を例示する。

sentences.en: Imagine a clinic planning changes to a room in which visitors wait for appointments.
sentences.ja: 来訪者が診察を待つ部屋の変更を計画する診療所を想像しよう。

sentences.en: One member of the staff suggests reducing every source of sound in order to create a calm environment.
sentences.ja: ある職員は落ち着いた環境を作るため全音源を減らす提案をする。

sentences.en: Another points out that some visitors may need to hear announcements clearly in order to know when they are expected to move to another room.
sentences.ja: 別の職員は別室へ移動するべき時を知るため通知を明瞭に聞く必要のある来訪者もいると指摘する。

sentences.en: A quiet environment could consequently be experienced differently by someone who is uncertain about whether an important announcement can be heard.
sentences.ja: そこで重要通知が聞こえるか不確かな人には静かな環境が異なる形で経験され得る。

sentences.en: The staff consider distinguishing sounds that provide useful information from sounds that serve no necessary purpose in the waiting area.
sentences.ja: 職員は有用情報を提供する音と待合区域で必要目的を果たさない音を区別することを考える。

sentences.en: They also discuss whether visitors could obtain relevant information through more than one form of communication.
sentences.ja: 来訪者が複数の意思疎通形式で関連情報を得られるかも話し合う。

sentences.en: A written display might provide a useful alternative for some people, although it would not necessarily be accessible to every visitor.
sentences.ja: 書面表示は一部の人には有用な代替手段になり得るが全員に利用可能とは限らない。

sentences.en: The staff recognize that the effectiveness of an arrangement cannot be determined simply by counting the number of available signals.
sentences.ja: 仕組みの有効性は利用可能な合図数を数えるだけでは決められないと職員は認識する。

sentences.en: The fictional clinic considers asking visitors which information they need while waiting and what difficulties they might experience in obtaining it.
sentences.ja: 架空診療所は待機中に必要な情報と取得時に経験し得る困難を来訪者に尋ねることを検討する。

sentences.en: These questions concern the relationship between the physical environment and the activities the environment is intended to support.
sentences.ja: 問いは物理環境と環境が支えようとする活動の関係に関わる。

sentences.en: The example does not provide evidence about the medical effects of noise or establish a design suitable for actual clinics.
sentences.ja: 例は騒音の医学的影響の証拠を提供せず実際の診療所に適した設計を確立しない。

sentences.en: Such decisions would require appropriate professional assessment and attention to the needs of the people using the facility.
sentences.ja: その判断には適切な専門評価と施設利用者の必要への注意が求められる。

sentences.en: An environment can have measurable characteristics without those characteristics providing a complete description of every user's experience.
sentences.ja: 環境には測定可能な特性があっても、それらが全利用者の経験を完全に記述するとは限らない。

sentences.en: Useful design questions examine what people need to understand or accomplish while using a space.
sentences.ja: 有用な設計の問いは空間利用中に人々が理解・達成する必要があることを調べる。

sentences.en: A change that improves one feature may create an additional difficulty if the relationships among different activities are overlooked.
sentences.ja: 一特徴を改善する変更も異なる活動の関係が見落とされれば追加困難を生むかもしれない。

sentences.en: A quiet room becomes a reminder that comfort and access to information need to be considered together.
sentences.ja: 静かな部屋は快適さと情報アクセスを一緒に考える必要を思い出させる。

questions.prompt: Why might measurements alone be insufficient?
options: They always reveal every person's needs.
They are never useful to designers.
They may not reveal differences in visitors' experiences.
questions.explanation_ja: 体験の違いが分からない。

questions.prompt: What does one staff member suggest?
options: Providing medical treatment in the hallway.

questions.prompt: Why might quietness not fully address comfort?
options: All visitors necessarily prefer noisy rooms.
Announcements always require a crowded space.
The clinic intends to stop providing information.
Some visitors need to receive important announcements.
questions.explanation_ja: 必要な通知へのアクセス。

questions.prompt: What alternative form of communication is considered?
options: A larger room without any signs.

questions.prompt: Why is a written display not a universal solution?
options: Different visitors may have different access needs.
No visitor can read any text.

questions.prompt: What is insufficient for evaluating the arrangement?
options: Distinguishing useful sounds from other sounds.
questions.explanation_ja: 合図の数だけでは不十分。

options: Which medical treatment everyone should receive.
What information they need and how difficult it is to obtain.
Whether all clinics are equally quiet.
How to construct a new building.

questions.prompt: Why does the author qualify the example?
options: The fictional clinic proves a specific noise level is medically safe.
All real clinics must adopt the plan.
The example provides individual medical advice.
Actual design and medical effects require appropriate evaluation.
questions.explanation_ja: 医療・設計上の結論は未実証。

options: Quietness is always the only measure of comfort.
Designing a comfortable environment requires considering users' needs and access to information alongside physical features.
Every visitor needs an identical form of communication.
The number of signals alone determines design quality.
questions.explanation_ja: 環境と利用者の情報ニーズ。

grammar.focus: without asking visitors about their experiences
in order to know when they are expected
grammar.explanation_ja: in order toは目的、when節はknowの内容。

grammar.focus: although it would not necessarily be accessible
grammar.explanation_ja: althoughは譲歩、not necessarilyは部分否定。

grammar.focus: if the relationships among different activities are overlooked

paraphrases.source: People who describe the quality of a public environment may focus on features that can be measured or observed without asking visitors about their experiences.
paraphrases.rewrite: Designers may measure features without learning how visitors experience them.

paraphrases.source: Another points out that some visitors may need to hear announcements clearly in order to know when they are expected to move to another room.
paraphrases.rewrite: Some people need announcements to understand when to move.

paraphrases.source: A written display might provide a useful alternative for some people, although it would not necessarily be accessible to every visitor.
paraphrases.rewrite: A display could help some visitors without serving everyone equally.

paraphrases.source: A change that improves one feature may create an additional difficulty if the relationships among different activities are overlooked.
paraphrases.rewrite: An improvement can cause problems when important relationships are ignored.

discourse.role_ja: 測定情報の利点と限界。
重要通知の必要から静けさの意味へ。
表示の利点とアクセスの差。
架空例から実際の評価へ。

cloze.explanation_ja: 活動間の関係を見落とす。
